relationships.subject: pannexin-1
relationships.evidence_quote: promoting PIEZO2-dependent mechanotransduction and opening of Panx1 channels in the urothelium, with consequent ATP efflux into the suburothelial compartment.

relationships.subject: ATP
relationships.evidence_quote: The released ATP activates P2X3 receptors on suburothelial Aδ and C-fiber afferent endings, initiating action-potential discharge that encodes bladder fullness [35].

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1 activity enhances P2X-mediated afferent responses, providing a potentiating “gain” on purinergic input.

relationships.subject: resiniferatoxin
relationships.evidence_quote: intravesical desensitization of TRPV1-positive afferents with resiniferatoxin (RTX) is feasible, reduces SP/CGRP immunoreactivity, and modulates afferent-driven bladder activity

key_findings: Bladder trigone has three afferent classes: intraepithelial P2X3/TRPV1 fibers, subepithelial peptidergic plexuses, and encapsulated PIEZO-expressing corpuscular endings.
PIEZO2-Panx1-ATP-P2X3 signaling with TRPV1 potentiation encodes bladder fullness; P2X3 antagonists reduced frequency in OAB trials.
